## Mandatory context and boundaries
Read the parent epic first. Applicable owners: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md; docs/action-reuse.md; docs/testing-approach.md; docs/services/channels.md (communication/Jido bridge and provider contracts); docs/services/engine.md (history, admission, finalization and delivery). Read docs/documentation.md before documentation/skill edits, docs/services/system-config.md before credential fixtures, and local module @moduledoc before extending a helper. Apply code-quality for code and skill-creator for the skill.
Only test/ additions or backward-compatible support changes, lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex, and .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/** are authorized. Do not edit application modules, dependency source/pins, config, migrations, mix.exs, CI, or unrelated skills. Existing-test expectation changes require the testing handbook's explicit approval; this epic authorizes additive coverage, not changing expectations.
Use real bridges, NodeRouter, Engine admission/history/persistence and configured Agent execution. Only provider/LLM boundaries are faked. A production defect is a reported blocker with a reproducer; do not patch production, silently omit a scenario, weaken an assertion, or close the issue as complete.
Validation timing, failure handling and final gates are owned by docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Record executed commands/results in this issue. No new browser E2E is needed: this work adds test/developer infrastructure without changing a deployed UI journey. No commit/push/merge authorization is implied.

Parent epic: zaq-o9d

## Functional specification and files
Own test/zaq/channels/integration/delivery_failure_test.exs; add only needed backward-compatible fake scripting/completion diagnostics to existing support or the new drivers. Enumerate Registry.all/0.
Use exact operation/content match scripts so failure is applied to final answer delivery, not swallowed by an earlier typing/status call. Test:
- A failed final send records a failed provider attempt and does not claim a confirmed answer placement.
- A failed final edit when updates are supported leaves provider-visible prior content accurate and does not attach the unconfirmed replacement as delivered.
- Scripted successful send/edit returns the actual provider id and Engine confirmation connects the right canonical assistant record.
- Existing adapter retry/idempotency semantics are respected. Do not introduce a new automatic retry guarantee or assert incidental raw attempt counts.
- Unexpected provider method/operation/route fails loudly; failure evidence points to provider/connector/request.
- A failure in one connector/session cannot affect another session/provider's response script, mailbox, LLM observations, grants or transcript.
- Run sessions for different providers sequentially in one test module/fixture lifecycle and verify exact configuration restoration and process cleanup after both successful and failing setup/execution.
Use existing DeliveryDiagnostics selectively for failure triage; do not change its privacy defaults or introduce global always-on tracing.

## Tests to add before implementation
The cases above, plus regressions for script queues not consumed by incidental traffic and unhandled provider calls not returning permissive defaults. Use bounded callback/dispatch completion barriers; do not poll database state.
After complete processing, assert both the provider-side observable outcome and actual Engine persistence. Keep generated private execution persistence separate from confirmed transcript placement.
A genuine app bug becomes a tracked blocker/reproducer and scope discussion; this task cannot patch it or weaken tests to close.

## Branches/paths validated
Send/edit success/error, intermediate status/final update, retry outcomes where already implemented, cross-session pollution, cleanup on success/error, and observed versus confirmed delivery.

## Mocking plan
Only external provider/LLM response scripts. No internal stubs or replacement Engine confirmation. Reuse the real linked-device transport wrapper and existing local HTTP servers.

## Documentation
Document scripting syntax with one send-failure and one edit-failure example, event correlation, and how to read failure diagnostics in README.

## Action reuse assessment
Reuse existing provider request boundaries and DeliveryConfirmation/HistoryIngress outcomes; scripting and diagnostics are local-only test mechanisms. No new retry/resend business operation or Jido Action is introduced. Verification compares native requests/recipient state with canonical confirmation state.

## Done when
The full common suite remains green across all drivers after failure tests, fake scripts are strict, and configuration/process/DB state does not leak between provider scenarios.

comments.text: Implemented registry-wide terminal-send failure without a status id, terminal-edit failure after successful status creation, unconfirmed-history assertions, and per-connector script isolation. Actual native attempts plus Engine confirmation/placement are asserted. Added lifecycle tests for setup failure, sequential providers, exact configuration restoration and process teardown. Focused delivery tests: 9 passed; lifecycle tests: 2 passed. Script strictness/exhaustion tests pass. mix q passes. The separate Telegram policy/dedupe/thread reproductions remain visible and do not arise from failure scripting.
